tasks.short: Develop, approve and implement purchasing policies and contract procedures.

steps.what: Review existing policies, contract templates and audit findings.

loop.input: Selected policies, templates and findings with document versions.
loop.output: Policy change brief with source passages and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Require a source passage for every proposed gap; manager checks material findings.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unresolved conflicts go to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text policies describe overlapping controls in inconsistent language.

steps.what: Agree control requirements with finance, legal counsel and operational stakeholders.
Draft purchasing instructions, approval rules and contract procedures.

loop.input: Approved control requirements, current policy and controlled document template.
loop.output: Draft purchasing policy and a clause-level change log.
loop.check: Validate required sections, approval limits and citations; flag unsupported additions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved policy choices return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but explaining changed controls requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Review legal obligations, control conflicts and contract implications.
Approve policy changes, delegated authority and effective dates.
Configure purchasing limits, mandatory fields and approval routes in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Publish the approved policy and archive the superseded version.

tasks.design: A controlled policy workspace in the {DOCS} combines templates, version history and bounded extraction and drafting loops. Approval in the {WORKFLOW} releases the exact policy version for publication and separately gates changes to controls in the {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy choices cross departments, while document wording and purchasing controls are maintained separately. Existing templates reduce formatting work but do not resolve conflicting requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting document versions, approval records and configuration checks. Bounded models can propose cited changes for review.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing delegated authority, interpreting legal obligations and translating unusual controls into supported configuration remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: The manager balances control strength against operational friction and secures agreement when departments carry different risks.

ambition.what: Policy change impact assessments showing affected approval routes and contract templates.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling drafts and more time testing proposed controls with stakeholders. Existing approval rights remain unchanged; the manager can propose control experiments within delegated authority.

reach.task: Maintain approval routes and policy publication records.
reach.learn: Configuration dependencies, effective dating and rollback procedures.

reach.task: Test purchasing procedures against actual requisitions.
reach.learn: Exception sampling and the operational effects of approval thresholds.

evidence.claim: Versioned templates and configured approval routes can automate policy administration; policy choices still require judgement.
Bounded extraction and drafting can assist policy preparation, but this digest provides no documented procurement-policy implementation.

assumptions: A mid-size company has documented purchasing limits and a named policy approver.
Time shares are planning estimates, not measured observations. Drafting and stakeholder agreement outweigh routine administration.
Build ranges cover a first policy family using existing infrastructure; shared components can support later tasks.
GDPR applies to personal data in records. Consultation follows national rules where procedures affect employees.
unknowns: Which policy versions and approval limits are authoritative?
Can purchasing controls be configured and tested without custom development?
Who can approve policy changes and production configuration changes?
research_questions: Which policy clauses can be tested automatically against configured purchasing controls?
How reliably does cited extraction identify conflicting approval limits?
new_work: Review proposed wording and unsupported policy additions.
Maintain templates, source permissions and approval matrices.
Test configuration changes and check effective dates.
Handle exceptions where the published policy exceeds system capabilities.

tasks.short: Find potential suppliers and interview them about availability, capability and sales terms.

steps.what: Clarify specifications, volumes, delivery needs and acceptable commercial conditions.
Search supplier directories and websites for potential sources.

loop.input: Search brief and a fixed batch of directory results and supplier pages.
loop.output: Candidate supplier records with capabilities, source dates and evidence links.
loop.check: Validate fields and duplicate identities; require evidence for capability claims.
loop.stop: Process at most 30 supplied pages per batch with one repair pass; return gaps for manual search.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier descriptions are free text and use inconsistent capability terminology.

steps.what: Screen candidate suppliers and choose whom to interview.
Send interview invitations and arrange availability.
Interview suppliers about capacity, availability, terms and delivery risks.
Consolidate interview answers and written terms into a supplier comparison.

loop.input: Interview notes and written supplier terms against a fixed comparison schema.
loop.output: Cited comparison separating confirmed terms, indicative statements and missing answers.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units and dates with code; retain contradictions for review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per supplier; unresolved terms remain explicitly unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes and terms express availability and conditions in varied free text.

steps.what: Decide which suppliers progress to qualification or a request for quotation.

tasks.design: A supplier research register in the {PROCUREMENT} holds dated evidence from a fixed batch of directory results and supplier pages, extracted through a bounded loop. The {WORKFLOW} prepares invitations for approval, while a second bounded loop turns interview notes and written terms into a cited comparison.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier information is scattered, often stale and expressed in incompatible formats. Availability claims also require direct questioning.
tasks.enabler_now: Small extraction tools can now be built economically around existing supplier records. Structured forms and scheduling configuration handle much of the coordination.
tasks.still_hard: Discovering suppliers outside known directories, verifying real capacity and judging evasive answers remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The manager probes uncertainty, reads commercial intent and builds enough trust to obtain candid answers.

ambition.what: Interview preparation packs for occasional buyers in smaller operational departments.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time copying supplier claims and arranging meetings, leaving more time for probing interviews. The manager retains supplier progression decisions; approval rights do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Run supplier discovery and prepare qualification evidence.
reach.learn: Source freshness, capability verification and comparable commercial terms.

reach.task: Assess whether supplier ranges fit expected customer demand.
reach.learn: Assortment economics, seasonality and minimum-order exposure.

evidence.claim: Structured supplier records, scheduling and bounded extraction can reduce interview preparation and comparison work.
The digest reports Walmart supplier-negotiation results using Pactum; that case does not establish automated supplier discovery or interviews.

assumptions: Supplier directories and public websites are the OTHER system category in the search step.
Time shares are planning estimates. Human interviews remain the largest step, consistent with the supplied priors.
Research uses permitted sources and fixed batches; supplier statements remain unverified until checked.
Interview notes are sufficient; recording or transcription is not required.
Supplier contact data is handled under GDPR, with access and retention controls.
unknowns: Which directories and supplier data sources are available and permitted for reuse?
How current and complete are existing supplier records?
Which categories require site visits, samples or specialist qualification?
What information may be disclosed in invitations?
Can the current purchasing system hold evidence links and provisional supplier records?
research_questions: How often do source pages omit capacity, lead times or minimum-order conditions?
Which interview questions reveal material differences that written terms miss?
new_work: Review candidate suppliers and evidence freshness.
Approve outgoing invitations and disclosed requirements.
Resolve contradictory terms and missing answers.
Maintain extraction fields, directory access and duplicate controls.

tasks.short: Prepare a documented supplier award recommendation for board approval.

steps.what: Assemble final bids, tender requirements and approved evaluation criteria.
Check available budget and existing commitments in the {ERP}.
Normalize prices, quantities and commercial exceptions into a bid comparison.

loop.input: Final bid versions and the approved commercial comparison schema.
loop.output: Cited commercial fields and exceptions for deterministic cost calculations.
loop.check: Code checks totals, units, currencies and coverage; a buyer checks material exceptions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per bid; missing or conflicting terms block completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Commercial exclusions and conditions are embedded in free-text bid documents.

steps.what: Assess technical compliance, delivery capability and material risks.
Select the recommended award and document trade-offs and exceptions.
Prepare the board paper with costs, rationale, risks and supporting evidence.
Review the recommendation and approve, reject or attach conditions.
Record the board decision and its conditions against the purchasing case.

tasks.design: A case in the {PROCUREMENT} links versioned bids in the {DOCS} to budget data from the {ERP}; a bounded loop extracts commercial terms before code calculates comparable costs. A deterministic generator assembles the board paper from reviewed fields, and the {WORKFLOW} records the board's decision against the exact submitted version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bid formats vary, cost calculations are maintained separately from source documents, and board papers repeat information already gathered.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can populate a controlled comparison schema, while inexpensive custom code handles arithmetic, completeness checks and board templates.
tasks.still_hard: Technical suitability, contingent costs, disputed exclusions and the recommended commercial trade-off still need accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager explains why the preferred award is defensible and makes uncertainty visible to the board.

ambition.what: Pre-board award clinics showing cost sensitivities and unresolved conditions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling papers and more time challenging cost assumptions before submission. The board retains award approval, and the manager gains a repeatable way to request clarification before a case reaches it.

reach.task: Normalize bids and investigate commercial exceptions.
reach.learn: Whole-life costing, conditional discounts and evidence traceability.

reach.task: Maintain the award approval record and supporting versions.
reach.learn: Decision conditions, document version control and audit trails.

evidence.claim: Structured bid comparisons, deterministic calculations and document templates can automate much award-paper preparation.
The proposed extraction and approval design is an engineering estimate; the digest supplies no documented board-award preparation case.

assumptions: This task applies to awards that cross the company's board-approval threshold.
Time shares are planning estimates. Preparation is more changeable than the supplied human task label suggests.
The budget check reports availability and commitments; it does not grant spending approval.
The board paper uses recorded rationale and standard text, so its assembly needs no writing model.
Recording board approval does not issue a supplier award or sign a contract.
Confidential bids and personal contact details receive restricted access under GDPR.
unknowns: What thresholds and exceptions require board approval?
Which cost components and exchange-rate conventions must be compared?
Where are final bid versions and signed board decisions held?
Can budget commitments be read reliably from the finance system?
Which approvals must be repeated when a bid or recommendation changes?
research_questions: Which commercial exceptions most often change the preferred supplier?
Can required board-paper sections be populated entirely from reviewed case fields?
new_work: Review extracted exclusions and unusual commercial terms.
Maintain cost conventions, templates and approval thresholds.
Investigate stale budget data and incomplete submissions.
Reset approval when material inputs change and track board conditions.

tasks.short: Coordinate procurement staff, priorities and supply issues across buying and distribution.

steps.what: Review open requisitions, purchase orders and supplier issues.
Check stock, inbound deliveries and outbound fulfilment constraints.
Combine purchasing and fulfilment updates into the team work queue.
Set priorities using business impact, urgency and available capacity.
Discuss blockers, allocate work and coach staff through difficult cases.
Send agreed assignments, owners and due dates to the team.
Review overdue cases and decide interventions or escalation.

tasks.design: Configured reports from the {PROCUREMENT} and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed deterministic joins on the {DATA_PLATFORM} and a shared exception view in the {BI}. The manager records priorities and agreed assignments in the {WORKFLOW}, which sends notifications and flags missed dates using explicit rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Buying and fulfilment information sits in separate systems, while a spreadsheet and mailbox bridge the teams. Management conversations also contain context that transaction records omit.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard exports, configured reports and small integrations can provide a shared operational queue. Faster custom development makes company-specific identifiers and exception rules affordable to maintain.
tasks.still_hard: Matching order and item identifiers, distinguishing genuine urgency and balancing workload against development needs remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The manager resolves competing commitments, coaches staff and recognises when a visible delay hides a deeper capability or relationship problem.

ambition.what: A midday recovery-priority review for threatened deliveries.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting status and chasing routine updates, and more time on recovery decisions and coaching. Existing delegation limits remain; fresher information supports more frequent reprioritisation within them.

reach.task: Resolve supply exceptions before they delay fulfilment.
reach.learn: Inventory dependencies, recovery options and escalation thresholds.

reach.task: Maintain work-item identifiers and accurate action records.
reach.learn: Data reconciliation, ownership transitions and exception triage.

reach.task: Adjust replenishment priorities when demand or availability changes.
reach.learn: Stockout exposure, substitution options and commercial impact.

evidence.claim: Shared operational queues and rule-based reminders can reduce status collection while managers retain allocation and coaching decisions.
Structured operational data is sufficient for this design; no model loop or autonomous agent is needed.

assumptions: Time shares are planning estimates. Status gathering is substantial, but supervision and prioritisation remain human.
Existing reports provide purchasing and fulfilment status; cross-system joining requires code.
The queue uses operational due dates and commitments, with manager-entered work allocation.
Team availability is limited to necessary availability information without absence reasons.
GDPR applies. Employee consultation under national rules may be needed if visibility or monitoring changes.
Consent and access ranges include consultation where applicable; elapsed consultation can exceed the working-day estimate.
unknowns: Can purchasing and fulfilment records be joined through reliable identifiers?
How quickly do operational status changes reach each system?
Which workload information is already collected and visible to managers?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed queue?
Who can reprioritise buying and distribution work across departmental boundaries?
research_questions: Which exception signals predict a delivery problem early enough for useful intervention?
Which recurring status meetings can be shortened once the shared queue is trusted?
new_work: Resolve unmatched records and stale operational updates.
Maintain exception thresholds and notification recipients.
Review alert usefulness and remove repetitive alerts.
Maintain access, retention and consultation records where applicable.

role.altitude: The purchasing manager's week shifts from assembling status and approval papers toward supplier challenge, control design and recovery decisions. Board and executive approval limits stay in place; the manager can make better-supported decisions more frequently within existing authority.
reach: Help purchasing agents build comparable supplier evidence and investigate commercial exceptions.
Help procurement clerks maintain reliable approval records and operational queues.
Work with wholesale and retail buyers on availability, assortment and replenishment trade-offs.
skills_to_grow: Translate purchasing controls into testable rules and approval routes.
Assess whole-life costs and sensitivity to uncertain supplier terms.
Review cited model outputs and recognise missing evidence.
Understand operational identifiers, data freshness and access controls.
Coach staff and lead supplier conversations under uncertainty.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a shared procurement decision service combining supplier evidence, award preparation and early supply-risk reviews, while keeping commercial commitments with authorised people.
